new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Fully cooked, seasoned shredded pork sold in refrigerated heat-and-serve pouches (Del Real 15 oz, Curly's, store-brand carnitas), roughly $6-8/lb - a different product concept and price class from any raw pork cut, so it cannot reuse pork-loin, pork-shoulder or ground-pork, and it is not deli-ham or diced-ham. The pre-resolve table reports board ABSENT for the term: no commodity match and no capture match across the estate's three commodity namespaces, and no vocabulary row shares a core word with it. If the estate already prices a cooked pulled-pork product under another spelling (pulled-pork, carnitas, cooked-pork), alias to that instead - that pairing is exactly the word-order/synonym case audit-commodity-dupes cannot catch. This recipe's method puts 1/2 cup on each breast, 280 g at source scale and 980 g at the 14-serving batch, so a null here would pantry-price over 2 lb of meat.

registrar_rulings.reason: Not priced anywhere under another spelling: swept all three namespaces plus the live feed for carnitas/pulled/shredded/barbacoa/cooked pork and found no commodity id — the estate's only 'carnitas'/'pulled pork' strings are recipe SLUGS (slow-cooker-pork-carnitas-bowl etc.), not ids. Reuse of a raw cut is not merely unwise, it is mechanically impossible: pork-shoulder (priced $1.94/lb Sam's) excludes 'smoked','pulled','seasoned' and ground-pork excludes 'seasoned', so a Del Real 15 oz Seasoned Pork Carnitas pouch can never crown either — the estate has already ruled cooked pulled pork a different purchase from the raw cut. The one adjacent id, cooked-shredded-chicken ($0.3744/oz Aldi), is the exact product-class precedent (fully cooked heat-and-serve shredded meat, priced per oz) but excludes \bpork\b, so it cannot carry this food and cannot be the clone donor (self-block trap). Same food, different form => new id + allowlist pair. NAME ruling, separately: no vocabulary row resolves 'carnitas meat'; a new vocabulary row 'pork carnitas' with alias 'carnitas meat' is needed, and macros must come from a transcribed label — every FDC row on the pre-resolve shelf (babyfood meat sticks, frankfurter) is the wrong food.

macro_cross_check: Source publishes 714 cal / 22 carbs / 100 g protein per serving at 4 servings. Recomputed from the food DB at source scale (chicken 800 g, beans 850.5 g, adobo 5.3 g, mustard 60 g, ham 224 g, carnitas 280 g, pickles 160 g, Swiss 252 g): 3684 cal / 156 g carbs / 411 g protein total = 921 cal, 39 carbs, 102.9 g protein per serving. PROTEIN AGREES: 102.9 vs 100.0, +2.9%, well inside the 15% bar, which confirms the two each-weight calls that carry it (ham slices at 28 g and Swiss slices at 21 g) and the 280 g carnitas. Calories +29% and carbs +77% both trace to ONE line, and it is a settled one I did not re-derive: '2-15 oz cans black beans' is weighed 850.5 g, which is gross can weight (2 x 425 g) including packing liquid, but the recipe drains the beans into the dish. On the drained basis (about 253 g per 15 oz can, 506 g) the recipe recomputes to 843 cal / 24.6 carbs / 97.8 g protein per serving - the carb figure then lands on the source's 22 almost exactly, which is the tell that the source costed drained beans too. This matters beyond accuracy: at the gross basis the recipe reads 921 cal against this run's 450-800 ceiling and would be retired, and even drained it reads 843. Protein is 2.4x the 40 g floor either way. RECOMMENDATION: have the drained-can basis for '2-15 oz cans black beans' checked before the macro gate rules on this recipe; the residual weights are not what is pushing it over.
